court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Additional District and Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court, Tenkasi, C.M.A.No.53 of 2018
facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife. The marriage was solemnized on 30.08.1977. The respondent frequently quarreled with the petitioner upon suspicion of illegal contacts with several women. The case came to appeal against the judgment and decree passed in C.M.A.No.53 of 2018.

legal_principles.principle: Past incidents which have been condoned cannot be reversed.
legal_principles.held: it is clear that past incidents which have been condoned cannot be reversed and that there should not be any improper delay.

legal_principles.principle: The institution of civil suits by both parties will not be termed as cruelty.
legal_principles.held: the institution of civil suits by both parties will not be termed as cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: The trial Courts and the High Courts have no power to grant divorce on the ground of irretrievable break down of marriage.
legal_principles.held: the Hon’ble Supreme Court has clearly clarified and held that the trial Courts and the High Courts have no power to grant divorce on the ground of irretrievable break down of marriage
cited_cases: (2017) 4 Supreme Court Cases 85 in the case of 'Suman Singh /v/ Sanjay Singh'

outcome.final_order: The final court order set aside the decree and judgment passed in CMA.No.53 of 2018 and dismissed HMOP.No.157 of 2014.
